CITY OF INGLEWOOD

City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Assembly
Bill 361, please note that members of the public will only be allowed
to observe and address the Planning Commission of February 2, 2022
at 7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other means, as follows:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 3881092#

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:
   When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
   If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an area
  with good reception.
   If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the
  sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from the
  phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to feedback.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to Mindy
Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Planning Commission prior
to consideration of the agenda, comments must be received prior to
12:00 P.M. on February 2, 2022 the day of the meeting. Correspondence
should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 12:00 P.M. and prior to close of the public hearing will be
made part of the official public record of the meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California
90301.  All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours
prior to the day of the hearing.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FERUARY 2, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 2, 2022, in the City
Council Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner Patricia Patrick, the meeting
was called to order at 7:06 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Michael Pan, Acting Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager announced the division received one
item for Item 6A in support and copies have been distributed to
each of the Planning Commissioners and has been posted on-line.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
1) August 4, 2021 – Motion to Approve by Commissioner Patrick and
second by Commissioner Rice.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs.
Abstained: Commissioner Trejo

2) August 24, 2021 – Motion to Approve by Shaw-Williams and second
by Commissioner Trejo

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

3) September 1, 2021 – Motion to Approve by Commissioner Trejo and
second by Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 2, 2022

4) November 3, 2021 – Motion to Approve by Commissioner Patrick
and second by Commissioner Rice.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-013 (SP-2021-013) 3700 W. 102ND
STREET.
A public hearing to consider an application by Brian Kearney,
representing JSF Management, LLC, for Special Use Permit No. 2021-
013 (SP-2021-013) to allow: 1) construction of a new self-storage
facility; and 2) a reduced parking requirement through alternative
modes of transportation on an approximately 24,600 square-foot, M-
1L (Limited Manufacturing) zoned property in the Inglewood
International Business Park Specific Plan at 3700 West 102nd
Street.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff for clarification on the
location of the Storage building.
   Ms. Fewell responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Dana Sayles representing the JSF Development, along with Mr.
Brian Kearney spoke to the Planning Commission via telephone
regarding the project to answer questions from the Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant questions regarding –
multiple locations of the storage facilities in the Los Angeles
area, over saturation of storage facilities here in Inglewood
alone.
  - Ms. Sayles responded to Commissioner Patrick’s questions.
  - Ms. Wilcox also provided information related to Commissioner
  Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant questions regarding – if
they had received any opposition to this project, impressed with
how they reached out to the community and how many of the
community have signed in support.
  - Ms. Sayles responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant to explain what alternate
modes of transportation; how will 10 parking spaces be enough and
what are the benefits with less site parking?
  - Ms. Sayles responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked several questions of the
applicant regarding why place the Storage facility in a residential
area here in Inglewood and how many facilities does the applicant
have?

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 2, 2022
  - Ms.  Sayles  responded  to  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams’
  questions.

Chairman Springs asked several questions to staff and the Assistant
City Attorney regarding if the Planning Commissioners were to allow
the tenants in the area signature of approval as opposed to the
owners of properties in the area signatures, as it appears that
only renters signed their support for this project, along with if
the Planning Commissioners were to also accept the fact that the
majority of the signatures on these support lists appear to be the
same signature; also Chairman asked his colleagues their feelings
regarding the list of signatures, who may have signed or had their
names added by another individual and the fact that there appears
to be no property owner signatures, just tenants.
  - Assistant City Attorney Pan responded to Chairman Springs’
  questions, and Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo and Shaw-
  Williams responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs then asked the applicant what procedure was
conducted with regards to obtaining signatures from the residents.

Chairman Springs opened the phone lines to anyone wishing to speak
either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
Ms. Casandra Lozano, family member of one of the property owners
in the neighborhood, who is for this project.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any final
comments from the commissioners, hearing none, called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-137 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2021-013, subject to 12 conditions, and was seconded
by Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1918

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR
  BRIAN KEARNEY, REPRESENTING JSF MANAGEMENT,
  LLC, TO ALLOW 1) CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW SELF-
  STORAGE FACILITY; AND 2) A REDUCED PARKING
  REQUIREMENT THROUGH ALTERNATIVE MODES OF
  TRANSPORTATION ON AN APPROXIMATELY 24,600 SQ.-
  FT., M-1L (LIMITED MANUFACTURING) ZONED
  PROPERTY AT 3700 WEST 102ND STREET

Be approved

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, and Chairman Springs
Nays:  Commissioners Patrick and Shaw-Williams

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6B: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-014 (SP-2021-014), 1437 CENTINELA
AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Rob Searcy,
representing Fulsang Architecture for Verizon Wireless, for
Special Use Permit No. 2021-014 (SP-2021-014) to allow the location
of a new mono-eucalyptus tree wireless telecommunications facility
on an approximately 42,032 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial)
zoned property at 1437 Centinela Avenue.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 2, 2022
Commissioner Rice recused himself from Item 6B.

Ms. Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner, made the staff
presentation and made note of the revised design that the applicant
has submitted for the Commission’s review which is a more natural
tree shape.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff, there were none and he asked the applicant to
come forward to address the Planning Commission and speak about
their project.

Ms. Daisy Uy-Kimpang, Mr. Erik Fulsang – Architecture and Dave
Gonzalez of Verizon Wireless came forward and spoke to the Planning
Commission regarding his project on Plymouth Street.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant several questions, to
explain how will they handle traffic in the area while installing
the apparatus and keeping the traffic flowing, location of
ancillary equipment at the site and how tall and why?
  - Mr. Fulsang responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant what will be the benefits
of 5G and with this antenna and who will benefit?
  - Ms. Daisy Uy-Kimpang, and Mr. Erik Fulsang responded to the
  questions from Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant regarding the
maintenance of these types of mono-eucalyptus trees, fading, prong
durability and replacements.
   Mr.  Fulsang  responded  to  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams
  questions.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant several questions regarding
ownership of the equipment that they are installing, what is the
true reason for installing at that location, does it have to do
with Verizon customers having poor service. Next, are there other
mono-eucalyptus trees throughout Inglewood, and with the removal
of material from the other location, will that leave the old area
in a disheveled state?
   Mr. Fulsang and Ms. Uy-Kimpang responded to Commissioner
  Shaw-Williams questions.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final questions or comments from the commissioners, seeing and
hearing none, Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-145 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2021-014 subject to the 20 conditions, and it was
seconded by Commissioner Trejo, Resolution 1919

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO ROB SEARCY,
  REPRESENTING FULSANG ARCHITECTURE FOR VERIZON
  WIRELESS, TO ALLOW THE LOCATION OF A NEW MONO-

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 2, 2022
  EUCALYPTUS TREE WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS
  FACILITY ON AN APPROXIMATELY 42,000 SQ.-FT.,
  C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 1437 CENTINELA AVENUE.

Be Approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
Recused:  Commissioner Rice.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

7A: DESIGN REVIEW 2021-005 (DR-2021-005).
A non-public hearing to consider an application by Brian Kearney,
representing JSF Management, LLC, for Design Review No. 2021-008
(DR-2021-008) to allow a six story self-storage facility on an
approximately 24,600 square-foot, M-1L (Limited Manufacturing)
zoned property in the Inglewood International Business Park
Specific Plan at 3700 West 102nd Street.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff, seeing none he called for the motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made the motion to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2022-003, and adopt the attached resolution
approving DR-2022-001, subject to the 8 conditions and was
seconded by Commissioner Rice, that Resolution No. 1904

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWEOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AN
  APPLICATION BY BRIAN KEARNEY, REPRESENTING JSF
  MANAGEMENT FOR DESIGN REVIEW (DR-2021-008) TO
  APPROVE THE CONSTRUCTION OF A SIX-STORY SELF-
  STORAGE FACILITY ON AN APPROXIMATELY 24,600
  SQ.-FT., M-1L (LIMITED MANUFACTURING) ZONED
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 3700 WEST 102ND STREET.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(8) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick –
 Wanted to encourage all to enjoy these next upcoming weeks here
  in Inglewood, and Super Bowl at the So-Fi Stadium, and stay
  safe.
  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 2, 2022
Commissioner Rice -
 Wanted to announce that the City will be having a small street
  festival on February 10th, 11th, and 12th, with the Taste of
  Inglewood, and if you stay later in the afternoon, we’ll have a
  small game of football, called the Super Bowl.

Commissioner Trejo -
 Wanted to say thank you to the Planning staff and to her Planning
  Commission colleagues for putting in the time to bring this City
  back to its luster as the City of Champions. It’s great to be
  able to say that I live in Inglewood, as there was a time when
  it wasn’t.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Thank you to the Planning Staff for the wonderful Birthday Card
  as it was very precious and I thoroughly enjoyed it, also wanted
  to say congratulations to a fellow Morningside High School
  alumni, Ms. Paula White for being the artist who created the
  art for the upcoming Street Festival and the Posters that are
  seen all over the City of Inglewood and Go Rams.

Chairman Springs -
 Wanted to say thank you to the Planning staff especially for
  sending him his Birthday Card, he is truly thankful also
  thankful to his Planning Commission Colleagues for all of the
  hard work and the many hours that were put in to make the City
  of Inglewood definitely the City of Champions once again, and
  after being a long time resident of Inglewood, I arrived here
  after being discharged from the service, and have been a proud
  resident ever since.
 Excited about the upcoming Super Bowl Event – Go Rams, and the
  Taste of Inglewood and we’re looking forward to the future of
  this Great City of Inglewood.

(10) ADJOURNMENT:
Chairman Springs wished everyone a good evening and adjourned
tonight’s meeting at 8:28pm.
